searchText: Sorry I mean no particular contract, just a test contract that uses `blockhash()` hmm, gotta try it myself - cc <@360491619402776577> I would be extremely suprised if that was to happen, especially since all clients seem to agree on i could be less than a 1% probability according to my abservation, but just let you know in case it happens to anyone else Is the probability near 0.004? (I guess you query the current block's hash or query N-257 one) This is the code in use: require(block.number - blockNumber <= 64, "block number too old"); bytes32 bh = blockhash(blockNumber); require(bh != bytes32(0), "failed to obtain blockhash"); // this is the error being caught And it is unlikely that blockNumber is current block since there was a long process after the block is produced and before the contract is called. Any other possibilities? Can't argue a lot about internal logic of an unknown program, but a formal `require(block.number > blockNumber, "just in case");` might reveal some not expected behavior. Like if the contract was called twice by another contract in the same transaction.
